On the Ground from INN
Here's a selection of stories, free to republish, that cover the effects on communities of decisions made by the federal government, as well as local and regional coverage of key electoral and political developments. Questions? Get in touch by sending an email to <mailto:andrew@inn.org|andrew@inn.org>.

The latest politics, elections, and effects of federal decisions stories from INN members.

How California's Next Governor Could Affect Latino Communities
San Francisco Public Press Published on 06/02/2026

California's gubernatorial primary sees 61 candidates vying for the top two spots in November's general election, with recent polls indicating a tight race among the leading contenders. The outcome remains uncertain, making for a highly anticipated decision today.

Republish

More candidates are using their personal wealth to campaign than ever before. Should voters care?
CalMatters Published on 06/01/2026
Beyond the high-profile gubernatorial race, a CalMatters analysis reveals a significant story unfolding in the millions spent by down-ballot candidates, raising questions about the influence of personal wealth in this record-breaking election. Voters will soon decide whether this self-funding signifies independence or an attempt to buy political power.

Republish


San Jose may rethink voting method for special elections
San José Spotlight Published on 05/30/2026
San Jose is revisiting ranked-choice voting for city elections, specifically to address the high costs of special elections for council vacancies. A proposed charter amendment could allow the city to implement this voting system.
